title: The Radiators of Anderlecht
premise: Felix Thackeray, a retired archivist living above a shuttered café in Anderlecht, has spent eleven years mailing postcards to her childhood home, which burned down in 2013 — letters addressed to the family that took her in and then erased her from their photographs. When Odile Vranckx, the last fluent speaker of a dying Brussels dialect, asks Felix to become her final student, Felix resists: learning the language means speaking again, and speaking means being known. As Odile's health fails, Felix uncovers the truth of the fire and the stranger in the photographs — her foster sister Marta, who set it accidentally while trying to destroy evidence of their guardian's abuse. In the end, Felix records Odile's last words, forgives Marta at the hospital where she now works as a night nurse, and delivers one final postcard by hand — to a person, not an address.
about_author: Elodie Galloway is the pen name of a former translator who spent a decade in Brussels' fading multilingual neighborhoods before turning to fiction. Her work explores the quiet violence of forgetting and the stubborn architecture of chosen families.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet her meticulous routine: postcards to a burned address, a notebook cataloguing everything she never told anyone. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness disguised as order. A neighbor's casual question — 'who do you write to?' — cracks the surface for the first time.

chapters.title: A Language with One Door Left
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ninety-one-year-old Odile Vranckx places an ad seeking 'one student, no more, no fewer,' determined to pass on Marollien before she dies. She interviews candidates and rejects them all until Felix appears at the door out of curiosity. Beat: two women recognizing each other's solitude without naming it.

chapters.title: Lessons in Refusal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Early lessons stall because Felix can read the language but refuses to speak it aloud; Odile diagnoses this as grief wearing grammar as armor. Flashbacks reveal fragments of the fire and the erased photographs. Beat: frustration curdling into tenderness as Odile refuses to give up on her.

chapters.title: What the Photographs Kept
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Sorting a donated estate archive, Felix finds a photo of her foster household — herself cropped out, a stranger named Marta standing where she should be. She begins hunting the archive's provenance. Beat: the past stops being abstract; the wound acquires a face and a name.

chapters.title: Odile's War
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Interwoven chapters of Odile's youth: hiding Marollien from occupiers, losing siblings to assimilation, choosing silence as survival. She recognizes Felix's silence as kin to her own. Beat: Odile decides Felix will be her student not despite her brokenness but because of it.

chapters.title: The Address That Burned
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following the photograph's trail, Felix learns the fire was arson-adjacent — set by Marta, her foster sister, destroying documents of their guardian's abuse, with Felix's bedroom the collateral loss. Beat: rage and relief collide; the erasure was protection, not rejection.

chapters.title: Words That Cost Something
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile's health collapses mid-lesson; in the hospital she makes Felix speak — really speak — reciting a Marollien lullaby at her bedside. Felix's voice breaks open the sealed inventory of unsaid things. Beat: catharsis through language; the first honest sentence between them.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Old Photographs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix tracks Marta to a night shift at Saint-Pierre hospital and watches her from the corridor, composing and discarding confrontations. She realizes forgiveness cannot be written on a postcard. Beat: dread giving way to resolve; the climax approaches as Odile worsens.

chapters.title: Last Speaker, First Word
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Odile nears death; Felix records her final stories in Marollien, becoming the language's second-to-last speaker, then its last inheritor. In the same week, Felix sits across from Marta and speaks the unsaid inventory aloud — accusation, grief, and finally forgiveness. Beat: everything converges; nothing is held back.

chapters.title: Delivered by Hand
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue-like. Months later, Felix teaches a small Saturday class in Marollien — three students, no more, no fewer — and mails her last postcard to no one. Instead she delivers a new letter by hand to Marta's door. Beat: belonging rebuilt from ash; memory kept alive by voice, not paper.
